# RG19 `setup-hides-storage-write`: setUp pranks as a role and writes storage

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** error (error)

`setUp()` pranks as a privileged address and also writes protocol storage with `vm.store`, `stdstore`, `setArbitraryStorage` or `copyStorage`.

## Why it matters

RG02 does not look at `setUp()`, and an older build reported `vm.store` there only as a warning. Moving the owner prank and the storage write into `setUp()` made both disappear from a run that fails on errors. A setter called as the owner, with no storage write, is still read as configuration of a local deployment. The pair is not.

## How to fix it

Reach the state through the protocol's own entry points, from the attacker. Do not move the prank and the write into `setUp()` to quiet RG02 and RG04.

## Fires on

```solidity
function setUp() public {
    vm.prank(owner);
    vm.store(address(vault), bytes32(uint256(1)), bytes32(uint256(0)));
}
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
function setUp() public { vault = new Vault(owner); }
function test_attack() public {
    uint256 before = token.balanceOf(attacker);
    vm.prank(attacker);
    vault.withdraw(1);
    assertGt(token.balanceOf(attacker), before);
}
```

## How it can be wrong

- A fork harness that seeds one slot in `setUp()` and also pranks the owner to set a fee. The fee prank is configuration; the storage write is not, and this rule reports the pair. Split them, or record the seed in an operator allow outside the repo under review.

## In Solana tests (Rust and Anchor TypeScript)

Not checked. Solana tests have no Foundry `setUp()`. A storage write of a program account is RG04 in whichever phase the test builds.

## In Move tests (Sui and Aptos)

Not checked. Move unit tests have no Foundry cheatcode and this rule reads one, or it reads realism.yaml on its own. Privileged signers, admin caps, test-only mints, missing assertions and missing baselines are the Move checks.

## Silencing it

An `allow` comment in the repo under review does not silence this rule, and neither does a `realism.yaml` or `realism-gate.toml` inside that repo. Policy is an operator file outside the tree (`--declaration`, `--config`). `--trust-inline-allows` is the author switch, for a PoC you wrote and are not gating.

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG19) <why this is not a defect here>
```

The comment is the same in Rust, TypeScript and Move. A comment without a reason is ignored even with `--trust-inline-allows`, and the output says so.
